## Goal

Send one artifact to a team and know who answered: expected respondents with personal links, waits for everyone, and respondent status, presence and attribution as data any page shows in its own design.

## Owned requirements

Close each with the check below, through the real public interface (README §3).

| ID | Requirement | Route | Concrete check |
|---|---|---|---|
| CO-01 | Expected respondents can be named for an artifact or share; locally each gets a personal link | I, B | Roster of five yields five links mapping to five viewers; roster changes are events |
| CO-02 | Wait conditions for "every expected respondent submitted" and "N submissions", with an event when the roster completes | I, C | Property test over interleavings: satisfied exactly when the last respondent submits, under `once` per-viewer and `epochs` |
| CO-03 | Respondent status (not opened, drafting, submitted) through a client hook, the host protocol and the CLI | B | Five simulated viewers in browsers move through states; hook, protocol and CLI agree |
| CO-04 | Presence through a client hook, with opt-in cursor and selection sharing as ephemeral, rate-limited traffic that is never stored | B | Cursors from three viewers reach each other within the rate; the ledger holds no presence rows; opting out stops sharing |
| CO-05 | Attribution of artifact-scoped fields (who and when) readable by the page | B | Two viewers edit a shared field; each sees the other's attribution |
| CO-07 | A visibility policy decides what viewers see of each other's status and presence; owners, agents and hosts always see respondent status | B | Each policy setting returns exactly what it promises to a viewer's hooks; the default is the one WP-31 records with Mirza |

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- expected respondents and personal links;
- "everyone answered" and count waits, and the roster-complete event;
- respondent-status and presence hooks, with protocol methods and CLI output;
- opt-in cursor and selection sharing over the existing streams;
- attribution on artifact-scoped fields;
- the visibility policy;
- team scenarios in the conformance kit.

Design detail for this package:

- The surface and the options (D123); the session settles names and semantics and records them as delegated decisions.
- Roster: people named by the host's stable viewer reference (`view/url`'s `viewer`, D104) and display name, or by email where a remote server sends invitations; locally one personal link per respondent.
- Waits: options include conditions such as `submitted:all` and `submitted:<N>`, defined under `once` per-viewer (D107) and `epochs` (D103), with an event when the roster completes.
- Hooks: options include `useRespondents()` and `usePresence()`; respondent status also through the host protocol and the CLI.
- Presence and cursors are ephemeral (D47): never stored, rate-limited and coalesced, and off unless the artifact opts in. The shell imposes no presence UI (D121).
- Attribution: who last changed each artifact-scoped field and when, readable by the page.
- Visibility (CO-07): owners, agents and hosts always see respondent status. What viewers see of each other by default is a *Deferred decision* for this package with Mirza; recommendation: private unless the artifact opts in.
- Team scenarios join the conformance kit (WP-12).

## Out of scope

- Real-time co-editing of text (the v1.x Yjs plugin)
- Kit components for teams (WP-19, KT-11)
- Mentions in comments (WP-20, CO-06)
- Roles and permissions beyond capability scopes

## Acceptance evidence

the CO checks; a five-viewer browser scenario; the ledger holds no presence.

Also: `pnpm check` green, diff reviewed, the progress report's evidence table complete for every owned requirement (README §3), the evidence matrix regenerated, docs and AGENTS.md current, and the report finalized after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- Presence must never reach the ledger or the event log: a test asserts it (CO-04).
- Roster waits are level- or edge-triggered like D103 and D107: property-test the interleavings.

## Handoff

Team forms and live team pages work end to end; WP-19 and WP-20 add the kit components and mentions on these hooks.
